sentences.zh: 是我爸，或者——要么跑五分钟一英里，要么蹲五年大牢。

sentences.zh: 所以我当时——我可是拼了命在跑。

sentences.zh: 不，那是——我20年前在军队的时候。

sentences.en: Or 25, yeah.

sentences.zh: 是啊，我们当时在列队跑步，你可不想掉队。

sentences.en: And I remember literally yelling from the back of formation, where's the fire?
sentences.zh: 我记得我当时在队伍后面大喊：着火了吗？

sentences.en: Because I'm like, why are we running so fast?
sentences.zh: 因为我在想，为什么要跑这么快？

sentences.en: And then I looked at my watch and I was like, that was the mile mark.
sentences.zh: 然后我看了看表，心想，那是英里标记点。

sentences.en: And that's five minutes.
sentences.zh: 刚好五分钟。

sentences.en: It was almost – it was like 5.05 or something.
sentences.zh: 差不多是5分05秒之类的。

sentences.en: I was like, Jesus ChriSt.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 那真的非常、非常快。

sentences.en: So you – and I know, Zach, last week we spent a bunch of time talking about – telling me about your army pass.
sentences.zh: 所以你——我知道，扎克，上周我们花了很多时间聊——你跟我讲了你的军旅生涯。

sentences.en: But I don't know that – I know this detail.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道——我不知道这个细节。

sentences.en: Did you go to college in the army or army then college?
sentences.zh: 你是先上大学再参军，还是先参军再上大学？

sentences.en: No, I was in the college – well, so I was in college and then I kind of dropped out and I was – did a bunch of stuff including being in the army.
sentences.zh: 不，我当时在读大学——嗯，我读了一半退学了，然后做了很多事，包括参军。

sentences.en: So it took me 11 years to get through undergrad like from beginning to end.
sentences.zh: 所以我花了11年才读完本科，从头到尾。

sentences.en: I started in 92 and I ended in 2003.
sentences.zh: 我92年开始，2003年结束。

sentences.en: So a lot of people like my age have been working a lot longer than I have and then a lot of people much younger than me have about the same seniority that I do.
sentences.zh: 所以很多像我这个年纪的人工作时间比我长得多，而很多比我年轻得多的人资历却跟我差不多。

sentences.en: It's kind of an odd thing.
sentences.zh: 这挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: But yeah, that was just because like I was a really, really crap student and I didn't want to be in school.
sentences.zh: 但确实是因为我当时是个非常、非常烂的学生，我不想上学。

sentences.en: And I enjoyed the coursework.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢课程内容。

sentences.en: I just didn't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 我只是不想去学。

sentences.en: I just – I wanted to just like hang out and talk to people and have a good time and not do anything.
sentences.zh: 我只是——我只想闲逛，和人聊天，玩得开心，什么都不做。

sentences.en: I mean like – I mean that is the best part of university.
sentences.zh: 我是说——那可是大学里最棒的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean that – so that's the thing is that I feel like it's one of those things where I was given just enough freedom to be like, oh, why don't I just do this all the time?
sentences.zh: 我是说——这就是问题所在，我觉得我当时得到了足够的自由，以至于我想：哦，为什么我不一直这样呢？

sentences.en: And so then it turned into like my entire existence.
sentences.zh: 于是这就成了我生活的全部。

sentences.en: And so that was bad for like coursework and stuff.
sentences.zh: 这对学业什么的来说很糟糕。

sentences.en: But then eventually I kind of slept in the mud for three years and I was like, oh yeah, I like want a job job.
sentences.zh: 但后来我在泥地里睡了三年，我就想：哦，对了，我想要一份正经工作。

sentences.en: I don't want to do this.
sentences.zh: 我不想做这个。

sentences.en: I don't want to do anything like this.
sentences.zh: 我不想做任何类似这样的事。

sentences.en: So I became super student when I came back.
sentences.zh: 所以我回来后就成了超级学生。

sentences.en: I was on the dean list and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我上了院长名单，诸如此类的。

sentences.en: So yeah, it was good for me to have that as the sort of break that I had in the middle because if I just sort of worked at 7-Eleven or something,
sentences.zh: 所以，中间有那段休息对我来说是件好事，因为如果我只是在7-Eleven打工之类的，

sentences.en: I'd probably still be working there.
sentences.zh: 我可能现在还在那儿工作呢。

sentences.en: So I saw that you also – you went to UT Austin.
sentences.zh: 我看到你还——你去了德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校。

sentences.en: Was that both before and after the three years in the mud?
sentences.zh: 那是那三年泥地生活之前和之后都去了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And I went to UT Austin because I was from Houston and had one parent who lived in Austin.
sentences.zh: 我去德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校是因为我来自休斯顿，而且我有一个家长住在奥斯汀。

sentences.en: So I knew Austin.
sentences.zh: 所以我了解奥斯汀。

sentences.en: I knew I wanted to live there.
sentences.zh: 我知道我想住在那里。

sentences.en: I liked it a lot.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢那个地方。

sentences.en: I had friends from my high school that ended up there.
sentences.zh: 我高中时有朋友最后也去了那里。

sentences.en: And so I went there for like essentially social reasons and I just happened to be in a top five computer science department like with zero effort on my end.
sentences.zh: 所以我去那里基本上是出于社交原因，而且我刚好进了一个排名前五的计算机科学系，我几乎没费什么力气。

sentences.en: Like I was in the top ten of my graduating class and at the time that meant you had a push-button admission to any school in the UT system if you're a Texas graduating high school student.
sentences.zh: 当时我毕业班排名前十，这意味着如果你是德克萨斯州的高中毕业生，你可以直接被德克萨斯大学系统的任何学校录取。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So I literally filled out like a postcard and that was it.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的只是填了一张明信片，就这样。

sentences.en: And so like the fact that I got such a good computer science education was a complete accident but I'm really thankful for it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我能接受这么好的计算机科学教育完全是个意外，但我真的很感激。

sentences.en: I got a really good education.
sentences.zh: 我接受了非常好的教育。

sentences.en: Now did you know – were you doing computer science before you went into the Army?
sentences.zh: 那么你知道吗——你在参军之前就在学计算机科学了吗？

sentences.en: Like did you know when you went to college that's what you wanted to do?
sentences.zh: 比如你上大学时就知道那是你想做的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So I – well, the funny thing is like my entire childhood I wanted to be a physiciSt.
sentences.zh: 所以——嗯，有趣的是，我整个童年都想成为一名物理学家。

sentences.en: Like I saw these guys on NOVA on public TV and I was like I want to be one of those guys.
sentences.zh: 我在公共电视的NOVA节目上看到那些人，我就想成为他们那样的人。

sentences.en: I want to be a physiciSt.
sentences.zh: 我想成为一名物理学家。

sentences.en: But I was always obsessed with like space and astrophysics and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 但我一直痴迷于太空、天体物理学之类的东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, I like read a bunch of physics texts like in high school like just out of curiosity, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我高中时出于好奇读了很多物理教材，对吧？

sentences.en: And I would read physics papers sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我有时还会读物理论文。

sentences.en: I was like really into it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: And I remember at some point I was just messing around with my computer and I wanted to like do a little bit of programming and all the stuff I did was physics related.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次我只是在摆弄电脑，想做点编程，我做的所有东西都和物理有关。

sentences.en: But then when I was filling out this little postcard that I referred to before like there was a – well, you're in the College of Natural Sciences.
sentences.zh: 但后来当我填写我之前提到的那张小明信片时——嗯，你在自然科学学院。

sentences.en: There's one postcard and there's a different one for the College of Liberal Arts.
sentences.zh: 有一张明信片，文学院还有另一张。

sentences.en: And so I was in the Natural Sciences when there's a checkbox for each of the majors, right?
sentences.zh: 我在自然科学学院，每个专业都有一个复选框，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you get into UT, like you just pick your major.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你进了德克萨斯大学，你只需要选你的专业。

sentences.en: You get into one of those two schools like I said and you pick the major.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，你进入那两个学院之一，然后选择专业。

sentences.en: And I was looking at the checkboxes and I was like, oh, maybe I'll do computer science.
sentences.zh: 我看着那些复选框，心想，哦，也许我可以选计算机科学。

sentences.en: That's literally how long I thought about it.
sentences.zh: 我考虑的时间就这么长。

sentences.en: Because it was like physics, computer science, eh, why not?
sentences.zh: 因为当时就是物理、计算机科学，呃，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And so that's what I did to the major that I did, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我选择那个专业的原因，是的。

sentences.en: If you went into physics, you probably would have ended up in computer science anyways.
sentences.zh: 如果你选了物理，你可能最后还是会转到计算机科学。

sentences.en: Yeah, in a sense, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，从某种意义上说，绝对是。

sentences.en: Like so I've been working with some committee stuff with some people who are working physicists and they're trying to get things like SIMD stuff,
sentences.zh: 比如，我和一些委员会的人共事，他们是职业物理学家，他们正试图让一些东西标准化，比如SIMD，

sentences.en: standardized stuff for like linear algebra interfaces, standardized.
sentences.zh: 线性代数接口的标准化。

sentences.en: And so a lot of those folks are mathematicians or physicists and they do tons of like really rigorous computer science work as part of their job.
sentences.zh: 所以很多这样的人是数学家或物理学家，他们工作中做了大量非常严谨的计算机科学工作。

sentences.en: It's just the nature of the business.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个行业的本质。

sentences.en: Because if you work in any kind of applied math and if you work in any kind of physics these days, you know, your job as a programmer like more than it's not.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你现在从事任何应用数学或物理学工作，你知道，你的工作更多时候是在做程序员。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really sort of astonishing how over the past 30 to 40 years in almost all scientific fields, a large chunk of the field has moved to computational work.
sentences.zh: 是的，在过去30到40年里，几乎所有科学领域中，很大一部分工作都转向了计算工作，这确实令人惊讶。

sentences.en: But even for the chunk of the field that's still wet lab work where you're running physical experiments or something,
sentences.zh: 但即使对于那些仍然在湿实验室进行物理实验的领域，

sentences.en: increasingly there's a computational component to that work too because you're collecting so much data with these instruments that you have to do some post-processing of whatever actual experiments you're doing.
sentences.zh: 计算成分也越来越多，因为你通过这些仪器收集了大量数据，必须对你所做的实际实验进行后期处理。

sentences.en: And so it's like these days, like if you're in a career path where you want to study the sciences, you're probably going to end up having to do some programming.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，如果你走的是科学研究的职业道路，你很可能最终不得不做一些编程。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, so the first half of my career was at a research lab at UT called Applied Research Laboratories ARL.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我职业生涯的前半段是在德克萨斯大学的一个研究实验室，叫应用研究实验室（ARL）。

sentences.en: And I worked with a whole bunch of people on sonar and most of them were physicists who decided they didn't want to do physics anymore.
sentences.zh: 我和一群人研究声纳，他们大多数是决定不再做物理的物理学家。

sentences.en: One of whom was he said the reason he did sonar instead of cosmology is because sonar is so much harder.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人说，他做声纳而不是宇宙学的原因是声纳难得多。

sentences.en: Because it's a crazy, crazy hard thing to do because the noise propagation is incredibly noisy.
sentences.zh: 因为它是一件极其困难的事情，因为噪声传播非常嘈杂。

sentences.en: I mean, sound propagation is incredibly noisy and it's like you might as well just call it noise propagation.
sentences.zh: 我是说，声音传播非常嘈杂，你干脆叫它噪声传播算了。

sentences.en: It's all dealing with noise, whereas like you can get really good signals sometimes in cosmology and those tend to be the areas that people focus on.
sentences.zh: 这全是关于处理噪声，而宇宙学有时能得到非常好的信号，那些往往是人们关注的领域。

sentences.en: But yeah, it was interesting like dealing with like there was one project in particular.
sentences.zh: 但确实，处理这些事情很有趣，特别是有一个项目。

sentences.en: It was just me and this physicist, right?
sentences.zh: 当时只有我和这位物理学家，对吧？

sentences.en: So we had this Kalman tracker that we used to track signals and sonar data.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个卡尔曼追踪器，用来追踪声纳数据中的信号。

sentences.en: And with this old implementation, it was really crufty.
sentences.zh: 旧的实现非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Everybody's afraid to touch it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都怕去碰它。

sentences.en: And like we're going to do a fresh implementation of that from scratch.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要从零开始做一个全新的实现。

sentences.en: And I remember at one point, like we weren't doing a lot of object oriented programming for this.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次，我们并没有为此做太多的面向对象编程。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's numeric stuff.
sentences.zh: 显然，这都是些数字方面的东西。

sentences.en: And I don't really like, oh, anyway.
sentences.zh: 而且我其实不太喜欢，噢，总之。

sentences.en: And so he was he asked me at one point, what's this virtual?
sentences.zh: 有一次他问我，什么是虚函数？

sentences.en: What's virtual function?
sentences.zh: 什么是虚函数？

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, and I explained like, you know how you'd have like a bunch of different flavors of stuff and you have a switch statement.
sentences.zh: 我就解释说，你知道就像你有各种不同口味的东西，然后你会用一个 switch 语句。

sentences.en: It kind of gets rid of the switch statement and it goes all the way through and there's these problems with it and blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 它算是摆脱了 switch 语句，一路贯穿下来，但它也有一些问题，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And that was a little beyond what he can understand.
sentences.zh: 那对他来说有点太深奥了，他理解不了。

sentences.en: And so six months later, he's like, what is this virtual function?
sentences.zh: 所以六个月后，他又问，什么是虚函数？

sentences.en: And I did the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 于是我又把整套东西讲了一遍。

sentences.en: I explained it till we went into his office with chalkboard, explained the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 我一直解释，直到我们走进他的办公室，用黑板把整件事讲清楚。

sentences.en: And then a third time it happened about a year later.
sentences.zh: 然后大约一年后，第三次又发生了。

sentences.en: And I was like, Jim, I'm done.
sentences.zh: 我就说，吉姆，我受够了。

sentences.en: Like, this is it.
sentences.zh: 就这样了。

sentences.en: This is the last one.
sentences.zh: 这是最后一次。

sentences.en: Make take notes if you want to know what this is in the future or just live in ignorance.
sentences.zh: 如果你以后想知道这是什么，就记笔记，或者干脆就在无知中生活吧。

sentences.en: And I remember at one point, the same kind of thing happened, but the other way around.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次，同样的事情也发生了，但情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Like I asked about something I was kind of curious about, but it didn't stick.
sentences.zh: 比如我问了一些我有点好奇的事情，但没记住。

sentences.en: And I asked him about the same thing again.
sentences.zh: 我又问了他同样的事情。

sentences.en: He's like, I already explained this to you, like some physics thing.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不是已经给你解释过了吗，就像某种物理学的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's really funny how when people are technically oriented, whatever they're oriented towards,
sentences.zh: 很有趣的是，当人们有技术倾向时，无论他们倾向于什么，

sentences.en: the things that they're interested in stick in their heads really easily compared to other equally hard to understand things that are just outside of their interest area.
sentences.zh: 他们感兴趣的东西比其他同样难以理解但处于他们兴趣领域之外的东西更容易记在脑子里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so when when you sort of focus on one technical area, not another one, even if it's an adjacent area, a lot of times like there's there's a real lack of understanding.
sentences.zh: 所以当你专注于一个技术领域，而不是另一个领域时，即使是相邻的领域，很多时候也会出现真正的理解匮乏。

sentences.en: And it's not because these things are any harder to understand.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为这些东西更难理解。

sentences.en: So you're just not oriented towards doing that work to understand, you know, it's like that quote, the neurons that fire together, wire together.
sentences.zh: 只是你没有倾向于去做那种理解的工作，你知道，就像那句名言，一起激发的神经元会连接在一起。

sentences.en: It's like if you already have the vocabulary in your head, you know, learning something that's adjacent to that is super easy.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你脑子里已经有了词汇，学习与之相邻的东西就超级容易。

sentences.en: But if it's in some other domain that sure, it's just as hard, but you don't have the vocabulary, you don't have the wires that can fire together.
sentences.zh: 但如果它在另一个领域，当然，它同样很难，但你没有词汇，你没有可以一起激发的神经连接。

sentences.en: So it's just, it's, you know, I remember like so many things I've learned.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我记得我学过的很多东西。

sentences.en: Like I went through a finance phase where I wanted to be a quant and like they just have the vocabulary, the jargon that they have, like share, stock, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如我经历过一个金融阶段，我想成为一名量化分析师，他们有那种词汇，那种行话，比如股票、份额，你知道，

sentences.en: you get into options and stuff, derivatives, exotic.
sentences.zh: 你开始接触期权之类的东西，衍生品，奇异衍生品。

sentences.en: Like, it's just like, you have to learn this whole vocabulary firSt.
sentences.zh: 就像，你必须先学习整套词汇。

sentences.en: And like, if you, I remember asking my parents, man, like, what's the, what's the difference between like a stock and a share?
sentences.zh: 我记得我问过我父母，天哪，股票和份额之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: And like, they didn't, they didn't know.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道。

sentences.en: And, uh, and it's like, it's such a subtle thing, but it's not difficult.
sentences.zh: 而且，这是一种很微妙的东西，但并不难。

sentences.en: It's just, you need, you need to have the vocabulary in order to, to really grok.
sentences.zh: 只是，你需要掌握词汇才能真正领会。

sentences.en: If someone's explaining something to you, if, if every fourth word is like, I don't know what that means, then it's not going to stick.
sentences.zh: 如果有人在向你解释某事，如果每四个词里就有一个你不知道是什么意思，那你就记不住。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that's, that's, that's a, it's a huge problem for a software engineering education because, uh, we, we have, I mean, every field has its own language,
sentences.zh: 我认为这对软件工程教育来说是一个巨大的问题，因为，每个领域都有自己的语言，

sentences.en: but I think we in particular have a lot of jargon.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们特别有很多行话。

sentences.en: Um, and I think that, uh, it becomes so natural to us that we don't even realize, uh, how unapproachable it is to, uh, to newcomers.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这对我们来说变得如此自然，以至于我们甚至没有意识到它对新人来说是多么难以接近。

sentences.en: And the way it's taught is like, like I was, who was I just talking to this the other day?
sentences.zh: 而且它的教学方式，就像我，我前几天刚和谁在谈论这个？

sentences.en: The polymorphism, like in school, it's just talk like when they teach polymorphism, the unit in whatever engineering 201, uh, software engineering 201,
sentences.zh: 多态性，在学校里，当他们教多态性时，在软件工程 201 课程的那个单元里，

sentences.en: they just teach like runtime polymorphism, which also is known as dynamic polymorphism.
sentences.zh: 他们只教运行时多态，也就是动态多态。

sentences.en: But like there are, I think we, I listed off like 10 different types, static polymorphism, also known as compile time polymorphism, ad hoc polymorphism, parametric polymorphism,
sentences.zh: 但我列举了大约 10 种不同的类型，静态多态，也称为编译时多态，特设多态，参数多态，

sentences.en: like rank polymorphism.
sentences.zh: 比如秩多态。

sentences.en: It just goes on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 它没完没了。

sentences.en: But in school they own, like they refer to polymorphism and it just refers to dynamic, but there's like literally 10 different types.
sentences.zh: 但在学校里，他们只提到多态，指的只是动态多态，但实际上有 10 种不同的类型。

sentences.en: And I've never seen a talk that talks about like the umbrella world, you know, here's an umbrella term polymorphism and all the different types.
sentences.zh: 我从来没见过一个讲座是讲伞状术语的，你知道，这是一个伞状术语“多态”，以及所有不同的类型。

sentences.en: And I remember in an interview, I got asked once, what is static polymorphism?
sentences.zh: 我记得在一次面试中，我被问到，什么是静态多态？

sentences.en: Uh, and then I was like, ah, I think that's like, I think that's like templates.
sentences.zh: 我就说，啊，我想那就像是模板吧。

sentences.en: And they were like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们说，是的。

sentences.en: Uh, and they're like, so why is it called static polymorphism?
sentences.zh: 他们又问，那为什么叫静态多态？

sentences.en: I was like, listen, I don't know much about templates.
sentences.zh: 我说，听着，我对模板了解不多。

sentences.en: Like, uh, I just started learning C++.
sentences.zh: 我刚开始学习 C++。

sentences.en: And, uh, anyways, it's just, yeah, like the vocabulary problem is, it's, it's a problem because even in education, like they, they teach things in a very, very,
sentences.zh: 总之，词汇问题确实是个问题，因为即使在教育中，他们教东西的方式也非常，

sentences.en: I wouldn't even say it's simplified.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不会说它是简化的。

sentences.en: Like, I think that's misleading to teach the word polymorphism and not start off by saying, okay, we're going to focus on this one type,
sentences.zh: 我认为教“多态”这个词而不从一开始就说“好吧，我们要专注于这一种类型”是具有误导性的，

sentences.en: but like there are 12 different other types that you're going to get to depending on the language you work in.
sentences.zh: 因为根据你使用的语言，还有 12 种其他类型你会接触到。

sentences.en: And I think that's really true, especially in the light of the fact that, you know, there is lots of use for polymorphism in code.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是非常正确的，特别考虑到代码中有很多多态性的用途。

sentences.en: So there's very seldom a need for dynamic polymorphism in code, right?
sentences.zh: 所以代码中很少需要动态多态，对吧？

sentences.en: And so like very often I see people do stuff that are, you know, the kind of intermediate prograMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常看到人们做一些事情，你知道，那种中级程序员。

sentences.en: I work with a lot of programmers that are like that.
sentences.zh: 我和很多那样的程序员一起工作。

sentences.en: And it's not a failing of theirs is that they came from double E and they're kind of learning on the job.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们的失败，而是他们来自电子工程背景，正在边做边学。

sentences.en: And so it's another, it's another question of, of, um, focus.
sentences.zh: 所以这是另一个关于专注的问题。

sentences.en: And so when, when they, when they see a new programming technique, they aren't like really interested in drilling down on that.
sentences.zh: 当他们看到一种新的编程技术时，他们并没有真正兴趣去深入钻研。

sentences.en: That's what they're, they become obsessed with for a while.
sentences.zh: 那是他们暂时沉迷的东西。

sentences.en: They're like, oh, someone did a different way.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，噢，有人用了不同的方法。

sentences.en: I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm getting my work done this way.
sentences.zh: 我正用这种方式完成我的工作。

sentences.en: That's the important part.
sentences.zh: 那才是重要的部分。

sentences.en: The way that I'm used to doing it, how can I perfect whatever direction I'm already in?
sentences.zh: 我习惯的那种方式，我该如何完善我已经在做的方向？

sentences.en: So they already know like, oh, type stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以他们已经知道，噢，类型之类的东西。

sentences.en: They write lots of virtual functions, even when that's not necessarily the right tool for the job.
sentences.zh: 他们写了很多虚函数，即使那不一定是完成工作的正确工具。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, it's one of the things I just mentioned, not liking, oh, but I think that's like really big deal in our industry.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是我刚才提到的我不喜欢的事情之一，但我认为这在我们的行业中是一个大问题。

sentences.en: That there's so many people that even now, if you look like on online courses, like, you know, introductory stuff for C++ people, there's no good learning resources for C++.
sentences.zh: 即使现在，如果你看在线课程，比如 C++ 的入门内容，也没有好的 C++ 学习资源。

sentences.en: That's a different topic, but what there is out there, a lot of it's, uh, very focused on the same kind of overlap with,
sentences.zh: 那是另一个话题，但现有的很多内容，很大程度上都集中在与，

sentences.en: I'm sure other courses that the same people are making for other languages.
sentences.zh: 我相信同样的人为其他语言制作的课程也有同样的重叠。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that includes like lots of ideas from Java and other things that like sort of, um, co-evolved with C++ in the early days.
sentences.zh: 这包括很多来自 Java 和其他在早期与 C++ 共同演化的东西的想法。

sentences.en: But, uh, those people running those tutorials have no idea that like the, the sort of cognoscenti within C++ have completely moved away from that paradigm.
sentences.zh: 但是，那些运行教程的人根本不知道 C++ 内部的行家已经完全抛弃了那种范式。

sentences.en: And that's seldom used, except sometimes as an implementation detail of something else.
sentences.zh: 而且它很少被使用，除非有时作为其他东西的实现细节。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, it's, it's really kind of, it's kind of unfortunate because I think a lot of people reach for that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很不幸，因为我认为很多人会去用它。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, the previous role I had at my current job, I did a lot of like internal training and, and like there was part of this thing called the quality team.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，我在目前工作的前一个职位上，做了很多内部培训，而且有一个叫质量团队的东西。

sentences.en: The whole idea was to like decrease the defect rate in our, in our code, which was kind of high.
sentences.zh: 整个想法是降低我们代码中的缺陷率，当时缺陷率有点高。

sentences.en: Well, tragically high.
sentences.zh: 嗯，高得离谱。

sentences.en: It was awful.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so we were trying to get rid of like, you know, crashes at customer sites and stuff like this.
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图摆脱客户现场的崩溃之类的问题。

sentences.en: So one of the, one of the things my, my boss and I were talking about when I was first, uh, joined the team was he was like, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以当我刚加入团队时，我和老板谈论的事情之一就是，他说，你知道，

sentences.en: maybe we could do some internal training about this or that.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以做一些关于这个或那个的内部培训。

sentences.en: What do you think about putting together?
sentences.zh: 你觉得整理一下怎么样？

sentences.en: Like, like, like a, a course from first principles, like how to write code.
sentences.zh: 比如，从第一性原理出发的课程，比如如何编写代码。

sentences.en: Well, like, you know, good object oriented techniques.
sentences.zh: 嗯，比如，你知道，好的面向对象技术。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, that's, it's funny that you say that because there's no such thing.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，你说这个很有趣，因为根本没有那种东西。

sentences.en: His head kind of exploded.
sentences.zh: 他的脑袋差点炸了。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, um, he was great about like recognizing like, um, new material when I would present to him like new techniques and why they were important.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但你知道，当我会向他展示新材料和新技术的必要性时，他非常善于识别这些内容。

sentences.en: And he really took a lot of those, those lessons on board and that, that was really cool.
sentences.zh: 他确实吸收了很多这些教训，这真的很酷。

sentences.en: So he wasn't like pushing back against that.
sentences.zh: 所以他并没有抵制这些。

sentences.en: He was just surprised by it.
sentences.zh: 他只是感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And that reflects like an older mentality.
sentences.zh: 这反映了一种旧的心态。

sentences.en: Cause when he was a day-to-day practitioner, that was kind of the way you did things.
sentences.zh: 因为当他还是日常从业者时，那就是做事的方式。

sentences.en: Um, and unfortunately that has persisted,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这种情况一直持续着，

sentences.en: especially as like people that were from that era moving to management and then people below them are trying to do something a certain way.
sentences.zh: 特别是当那个时代的人转入管理层，而他们下面的人试图以某种方式做事时。

sentences.en: They're like, oh, you want to do an object oriented thing with like some big class diagram or something.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，噢，你想用一些大的类图之类的东西来做面向对象的事情。

sentences.en: And so that, that tends to perpetuate it.
sentences.zh: 所以这往往会延续下去。

sentences.en: And I'm kind of waiting for people to like, I know no one's going to read EOP, but I'm ready for people to.
sentences.zh: 我正在等待人们，我知道没人会读《编程要素》(EOP)，但我准备好让人们去读了。

sentences.en: So adapt those, those kind of, or adopt, I should say, those kind of, um, those kind of approaches, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以采用那些，我应该说，采用那些方法，你知道。

sentences.en: And that's, uh, that's Elements of Programming, which is, uh, Stepanov's, uh, uh, book, which is sort of the.
sentences.zh: 那就是《编程要素》，是 Stepanov 的书，这算是。

sentences.en: It's, it might not be the best book about computer science ever written, but it's the best one I've ever read.
sentences.zh: 它可能不是有史以来写得最好的计算机科学书籍，但它是我读过的最好的一本。

sentences.en: It's the, it's the only book on computer science or programming that I've ever read.
sentences.zh: 这是我读过的唯一一本关于计算机科学或编程的书。

sentences.en: I think we've talked in this podcast before about how I'm not a huge fan of like.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在这个播客里之前谈过我不怎么喜欢那种。

sentences.en: Wait, didn't you, I thought you said that about SICP, which is the structure.
sentences.zh: 等等，你不是说《计算机程序的构造和解释》(SICP) 吗？

sentences.en: I, you know what, I, I've read parts of SICP.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道吗，我读过 SICP 的部分内容。

sentences.en: I've, Elements of Programming is the only programming book I've read all the way through.
sentences.zh: 《编程要素》是我从头到尾读完的唯一一本编程书。

sentences.en: Like those are the two that I've read from, like, and not just like skimmed the index of, um, uh, and, uh, Elements of Programming is the only one that I've read.
sentences.zh: 就像那两本是我读过的，不仅仅是浏览过索引的，而且，《编程要素》是我读过的唯一一本。

sentences.en: I've actually read through it twice.
sentences.zh: 我实际上已经读了两遍了。

sentences.en: So I, I've read lots of them and I really think Elements of Programming is the one that, that I appreciate the moSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我读过很多书，我真的认为《编程要素》是我最欣赏的一本。

sentences.en: And in fact, what I often tell people is, you know, you get us a free PDF download these days.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我经常告诉人们的是，你知道，现在你可以免费下载 PDF。

sentences.en: Like you don't even need to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不需要付钱。

sentences.en: You don't even need to hold around a dead tree in your hands, right?
sentences.zh: 你甚至不需要手里拿着一本死树书，对吧？

sentences.en: All you need to do is like go and download it from somewhere.
sentences.zh: 你所要做的就是从某个地方下载它。

sentences.en: But if you can internalize the first six pages of the first, um, of the first pair, I mean the first chapter, that's all you need.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能内化第一章的前六页，那就是你所需要的全部。

sentences.en: Literally the first six pages.
sentences.zh: 字面上就是前六页。

sentences.en: If you can internalize that, the rest of it is logical extension of that first six pages.
sentences.zh: 如果你能内化它，剩下的就是那前六页的逻辑延伸。

sentences.en: If, if you apply those first six pages to all these kinds of programming styles that are, that are covered in the rest of the book, that's where the rest of the book comes from.
sentences.zh: 如果你把那前六页应用到书中涵盖的所有这些编程风格中，这就是书的其余部分来源。

sentences.en: And the rest of the book is very dense and hard to get through.
sentences.zh: 书的其余部分非常密集，很难读完。

sentences.en: That first six pages is also dense and hard to get you, but it's only six pages.
sentences.zh: 那前六页也很密集，很难读，但只有六页。

sentences.en: So it's worth, you know, a time investment.
sentences.zh: 所以值得投入时间。

sentences.en: I always tell people that I don't think I've had any takers, but I mean, the stuff in that first six pages is so good.
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉人们，我不认为有人采纳了，但我的意思是，那前六页里的东西太棒了。

sentences.en: You know, I don't know if you guys had a similar experience of like, you know, when I was first starting out, I would,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不知道你们是否有类似的经历，你知道，当我刚开始的时候，我会，

sentences.en: hear about some technique and I would like be like, I'm going to find an excuse to use my code.
sentences.zh: 听说某种技术，我会想，我要找个借口在我的代码中使用它。

sentences.en: Cause that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 因为那很有趣。

sentences.en: I'm going to see if that works.
sentences.zh: 我要看看它是否有效。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so you do things like kind of like the wrong way on purpose to see how it worked.
sentences.zh: 所以你会故意用错误的方式做事情，看看它是如何工作的。

sentences.en: And then you're like, ah, it works or it didn't.
sentences.zh: 然后你会说，啊，它成功了或者没成功。

sentences.en: And you kind of adapt.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会适应。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there've been many, many different styles of like things from like, you know, just texting, text, textual conventions, like, you know, where you put hanging braces,
sentences.zh: 所以有很多很多不同的风格，从文本约定，比如，你知道，你在哪里放悬挂花括号，

sentences.en: all these different things I've tried over the course of my career over and over again, different experiments.
sentences.zh: 所有这些不同的事情，我在我的职业生涯中一遍又一遍地尝试，不同的实验。

sentences.en: And the only bit of advice that I have, once I internalized it, I literally never looked back or never changed.
sentences.zh: 我唯一的建议是，一旦我内化了它，我真的从未回头或从未改变。

sentences.en: Even when I was, had new, new data introduced to me as those first six pages of that first chapter.
sentences.zh: 即使当我有了新的数据被介绍给我时，那也是第一章的前六页。

sentences.en: I mean, they're, they're really, I think unassailable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为它们真的是无可辩驳的。

sentences.en: What are the, what are the key lessons to take away from?
sentences.zh: 要从中吸取的关键教训是什么？

sentences.en: Um, so, so some of the key lessons, um, are things that people already pretty well understand.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，一些关键的教训，是人们已经相当了解的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, so one of the things is, um, you know, you want to write things for, for reuse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以其中一点是，你知道，你希望为了复用而编写代码。

sentences.en: And that means like writing things generically.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要以通用的方式编写代码。

sentences.en: Um, there's lots of things about like, um, defining what should and should not be in interfaces.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于定义接口中应该包含什么和不应该包含什么，有很多讲究。

sentences.en: And this is the part that I think people don't take on board as well.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是人们没有很好地领会的部分。

sentences.en: Um, one thing in particular is that, you know, they, they define what a basis of operations is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别重要的一点是，他们定义了什么是操作基准。

sentences.en: A basis is, it takes its name as analogy to like, uh, basis vectors in an, in an N space, right?
sentences.zh: “基准”这个词取自类比，就像 N 维空间中的基向量一样，对吧？

sentences.en: So you have N basis vectors that are worth their normal, and then that defines an N space.
sentences.zh: 所以你有 N 个基向量，它们是正交的，然后这就定义了一个 N 维空间。

sentences.en: Similarly, you can define N operations on your type.
sentences.zh: 同样地，你也可以在你的类型上定义 N 个操作。

sentences.en: And as long as those N operations on the type are defined, you can do anything that that type is capable of just with some combination of those.
sentences.zh: 只要定义了这 N 个操作，你就可以仅通过它们的某种组合来完成该类型所能做的任何事情。

sentences.en: And as long as you can efficiently get to any behavior you want to using those types, and that's the right, or sorry, that those, uh, those operations,
sentences.zh: 只要你能利用这些类型，或者说抱歉，利用这些操作，高效地实现你想要的任何行为，

sentences.en: that's the right set of operations.
sentences.zh: 那这就是正确的一组操作。

sentences.en: And you don't want any more operations than that, because that increases test burden, surface area, it creates confusion, all kinds of stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 而且你不需要比这更多的操作，因为那会增加测试负担、扩大接口表面积、造成混乱，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So you want it to be small, but not too small.
sentences.zh: 所以你希望它小巧，但又不能太小。

sentences.en: You want it to be efficient.
sentences.zh: 你希望它高效。

sentences.en: And then as long as that exists, you can do anything else.
sentences.zh: 只要满足这些，你就可以做任何其他事情。

sentences.en: And the reason you don't want to add anything else is because if you write free functions instead of writing a new member, then when some other type, you've got your type T,
sentences.zh: 你不想添加任何其他东西的原因是，如果你编写自由函数而不是编写新的成员函数，那么当你有另一个类型 T 时，

sentences.en: some other type U, you write it in the future.
sentences.zh: 将来你编写了另一个类型 U。

sentences.en: And it has very similar semantics in some aspect of what this type T did.
sentences.zh: 并且它在某些方面与类型 T 的语义非常相似。

sentences.en: Then all of a sudden, that free function you wrote, you can just use it and it works, right?
sentences.zh: 那么突然之间，你编写的那个自由函数就可以直接拿来用，而且能正常工作，对吧？

sentences.en: This is the same idea behind the algorithms library by one of the same two people, right?
sentences.zh: 这和那两个人提出的算法库背后的理念是一样的，对吧？

sentences.en: Alex Stepanoff, Paul McJones being the other one.
sentences.zh: Alex Stepanoff，另一个是 Paul McJones。

sentences.en: The idea there was like, we're going to write all these algorithms and not like hang an algorithm off of all these different data structures like vector and map and so on.
sentences.zh: 那里的想法是，我们要编写所有这些算法，而不是把算法挂在 vector、map 等各种不同的数据结构上。

sentences.en: And I think that's the right way to do things.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是做事的正确方式。

sentences.en: And in fact, I really think after having gone through the process of adding a new container-like thing to the standard library, which is flat map,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在经历了向标准库添加像 flat map 这样类似容器的东西的过程后，我真的认为，

sentences.en: I realized that I don't ever want to do that again.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我再也不想做那种事了。

sentences.en: I don't want anyone else to have to do that again either because I think the right thing for something like flat map – well, let me back up.
sentences.zh: 我也不希望其他人不得不这样做，因为我认为对于像 flat map 这样的东西，正确的做法是——好吧，让我退一步说。

sentences.en: So what I'm talking about in particular is flat map because it's just, you know, cloning most of the interface of map.
sentences.zh: 我特别提到 flat map 是因为它只是，你知道，克隆了 map 的大部分接口。

sentences.en: It has things like insert, it has in place, it has the square bracket operator, it has try in place, it has blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 它有 insert、emplace、方括号运算符、try_emplace 等等。

sentences.en: It has all these different things, right?
sentences.zh: 它有所有这些不同的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: And if you boil it down, it's just try in place.
sentences.zh: 如果你归纳一下，其实就是 try_emplace。

sentences.en: Like literally, you can write try in place and all the others, like in their description, they say like,
sentences.zh: 字面上看，你可以写出 try_emplace，而其他所有函数，在它们的描述中都说，

sentences.en: we're going to do try in place and if that doesn't work, then we're going to create a new object and then we're going to try in place.
sentences.zh: 我们要执行 try_emplace，如果不行，那么我们就创建一个新对象，然后再尝试 emplace。

sentences.en: That's what square bracket is defined as, like roughly, right?
sentences.zh: 方括号运算符大致就是这样定义的，对吧？

sentences.en: And so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: Like all the other kind of inserts are just some permutation of try in place.
sentences.zh: 所有其他类型的 insert 基本上都是 try_emplace 的某种排列组合。

sentences.en: So that begs the question, if we have map, flat map, multi-map, flat multi-map, I guess the own order ones don't quite work the same.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个问题，如果我们有 map、flat map、multi-map、flat multi-map，我想无序容器可能不太一样。

sentences.en: But if we have that for the tree-like containers, even if you have a flattened tree in the case of flat map,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们对树状容器都有这些，即使在 flat map 的情况下是扁平化的树，

sentences.en: why don't we have just like a free function that does insert, that does in terms of try in place?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能只用一个自由函数来做 insert，通过 try_emplace 来实现呢？

sentences.en: And then if you want to make your own map-like type, you only have to define like, you know, 10, 12 functions, something like that,
sentences.zh: 然后如果你想创建自己的类 map 类型，你只需要定义大约 10 到 12 个函数，类似这样，

sentences.en: instead of like literally, I think for std vector, which is much smaller, I think there was 64 members.
sentences.zh: 而不是像 std vector 那样，虽然它小得多，但我记得有 64 个成员函数。

sentences.en: Yeah, and like most of them are some form of in place, push back, or yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且其中大多数都是某种形式的 emplace、push_back 之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So if you had in place and in place back, you know, that's all you really need, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有 emplace 和 emplace_back，你知道，这就是你真正需要的全部，对吧？

sentences.en: You can even have a branch inside of in place that tells that it's at the back and it does the right thing, right?
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在 emplace 内部加一个分支来判断它是否在末尾，然后做正确的事，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you know, that's a generalization that costs you some efficiency, so maybe you don't want that, but you could get there too.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一种以牺牲一些效率为代价的泛化，所以也许你不想那样做，但你也可以做到。

sentences.en: So the long and short of it is, I think people should be writing more containers, because like, let's say you've got vector and static vector and dynamic,
sentences.zh: 长话短说，我认为人们应该编写更多的容器，因为，假设你有 vector、static vector 和 dynamic，

sentences.en: or not dynamic vector, what am I trying to say?
sentences.zh: 或者不是 dynamic vector，我想说什么来着？

sentences.en: Small vector, right?
sentences.zh: Small vector，对吧？

sentences.en: That's what I'm trying to say.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想说的。

sentences.en: So small vector is the one with a small buffer optimization, then it goes to the heap if it can't do stuff there.
sentences.zh: 所以 small vector 是那种带有小缓冲区优化的容器，如果无法在缓冲区内完成操作，它就会转向堆内存。

sentences.en: You really want to be able to write all those really conveniently, right?
sentences.zh: 你确实希望能够非常方便地编写所有这些容器，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's no reason why you shouldn't have a vector-like interface for any of these things, but people don't have a convenient way of doing that.
sentences.zh: 因为没有理由不为所有这些东西提供类似 vector 的接口，但人们没有方便的方法来做到这一点。

sentences.en: They have to, like, repeat those 64 different ways of doing stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不重复那 64 种不同的做事方式。

sentences.en: So I think it's a big, fat bummer.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And David Stone, actually, he's another committee member.
sentences.zh: David Stone，实际上，他是另一位委员会成员。

sentences.en: He has a project that he's been working on for a little while to try to make the abstractions for all of the,
sentences.zh: 他有一个项目，他已经研究了一段时间，试图为所有这些东西建立抽象，

sentences.en: with sort of these sort of categories of containers and standard, right?
sentences.zh: 用标准中这类容器的分类，对吧？

sentences.en: So the vector-like ones are sequence containers, and the node-based containers are, what do we call those?
sentences.zh: 所以类似 vector 的是序列容器，而基于节点的容器是，我们称它们为什么？

sentences.en: We call them associated containers.
sentences.zh: 我们称它们为关联容器。

sentences.en: So those are things like map and set and so forth.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是像 map 和 set 之类的东西。

sentences.en: So he's tried to do exactly what I just talked about, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他试图做我刚才谈到的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, figuring out what that small basis is, and let's make free functions for everything else.
sentences.zh: 找出那个小的操作基准，然后为其他所有东西编写自由函数。

sentences.en: And he says he's still not happy with it.
sentences.zh: 他说他对此仍然不满意。

sentences.en: He's been working on it for a while.
sentences.zh: 他已经研究了一段时间了。

sentences.en: But I think that kind of thing, really, if people did more of that, then we would be better off.
sentences.zh: 但我认为那种事情，如果人们多做一些，我们就会过得更好。

sentences.en: So the classic example to me is, and this is a real question I had at work.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，经典的例子是，这是我在工作中遇到的一个真实问题。

sentences.en: Like, someone said, well, I got this string view, and it's got, like, find last not of or something.
sentences.zh: 有人说，我有这个 string_view，它有 find_last_not_of 之类的方法。

sentences.en: So one of these algorithms that hangs off of strings and string views.
sentences.zh: 所以这是挂在 string 和 string_view 上的算法之一。

sentences.en: And he said, but I've got a span sometimes.
sentences.zh: 他说，但我有时用的是 span。

sentences.en: Sometimes I've got a string view.
sentences.zh: 有时我用的是 string_view。

sentences.en: Like, how do I do this?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么做？

sentences.en: And I said, well, you have to construct a string view from the span in order to get that algorithm.
sentences.zh: 我说，你必须从 span 构造一个 string_view 才能使用那个算法。

sentences.en: It's dumb, but that's what you have to do.
sentences.zh: 这很蠢，但你只能这么做。

sentences.en: And that's such an unsatisfying answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人不满意的答案。

sentences.en: Like, why isn't that an algorithm, right?
sentences.zh: 为什么那不是一个算法呢，对吧？

sentences.en: And why don't we have just a set of string algorithms that does string stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能只拥有一套处理字符串的算法呢，对吧？

sentences.en: I think that could work really nice.
sentences.zh: 我认为那样会非常好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think once you learn more about generic programming, you start to become aware of the cost of adding a new type and of added complexity in the interface of a type.
sentences.zh: 我认为一旦你对泛型编程了解更多，你就会开始意识到添加新类型以及增加类型接口复杂性的代价。

sentences.en: And it's like any time, either worker on the committee, that somebody shows me, you know, their proposal for some new class does some great thing.
sentences.zh: 就像无论何时，在委员会工作时，有人向我展示他们关于某个新类的提案，说它能做某件伟大的事情。

sentences.en: And it's got, like, a lot of knobs and bells and whistles.
sentences.zh: 而且它有很多旋钮、铃铛和哨子（指复杂的功能）。

sentences.en: My, like, first gut reaction is always, like, all right, let's, like, take all those knobs and bells and whistles and, like, take them out.
sentences.zh: 我的第一反应总是，好吧，让我们把那些旋钮、铃铛和哨子都去掉。

sentences.en: And, like, let's just get down to, like, what are the core basis operations of this thing?
sentences.zh: 让我们回归到这个东西的核心操作基准是什么？

sentences.en: And it's because any time that we add additional complexity that we don't need, one, it's typically a mistake that we can't come back and undo later.
sentences.zh: 这是因为每当我们添加不必要的额外复杂性时，首先，这通常是一个我们以后无法撤销的错误。

sentences.en: But we end up in this world where we have things like string that have, you know, dozens of different operations on it.
sentences.zh: 但我们最终陷入了一个境地，我们有像 string 这样拥有几十种不同操作的东西。

sentences.en: And when we wanted to make another string-like thing, string view, we had no choice but to make string view have all those same operations as well.
sentences.zh: 当我们想制作另一个类似字符串的东西 string_view 时，我们别无选择，只能让 string_view 也拥有所有这些相同的操作。

sentences.en: And I think that that's a much worse world than the world that we could have lived in where we could have had some string algorithms and maybe we could have introduced some sort of concept for string types.
sentences.zh: 我认为这比我们本可以拥有的世界要糟糕得多，在那个世界里，我们可以拥有一些字符串算法，也许我们可以为字符串类型引入某种概念。

sentences.en: And we could have had some, like, string view would have looked a lot more like span.
sentences.zh: 我们可以让 string_view 看起来更像 span。

sentences.en: It would have been a very simple thing.
sentences.zh: 它本可以是一个非常简单的东西。

sentences.en: And it would have been possible to have, like, a string-like concept where you could just have your own string thing just satisfy that concept.
sentences.zh: 并且可以拥有一个类似字符串的概念，这样你就可以拥有自己的字符串类型，只需满足该概念即可。

sentences.en: But in the same vein as that, you know, when we added – I know a lot of people are happy that we're finally getting on std string in the last couple of standards we've gotten,
sentences.zh: 但同样地，你知道，当我们添加——我知道很多人很高兴我们在过去几个标准中终于在 std string 中得到了，

sentences.en: like, contained start with and ends with.
sentences.zh: 比如 starts_with 和 ends_with。

sentences.en: And I complained so loudly in LEWGA that we should not be adding these.
sentences.zh: 我在 LEWGA（库演进工作组）里大声抱怨过，我们不应该添加这些。

sentences.en: Like, these are algorithms that we should have with those names that work with strings.
sentences.zh: 这些应该是我们应该拥有的、以这些名字命名的、能处理字符串的算法。

sentences.en: And they said, but they don't work for char-star.
sentences.zh: 他们说，但它们不能处理 char*。

sentences.en: I'm saying, so let's make an overload that works for char-star.
sentences.zh: 我说，那就让我们做一个能处理 char* 的重载。

sentences.en: This is not hard to do.
sentences.zh: 这并不难做到。

sentences.en: We can add that, right?
sentences.zh: 我们可以添加它，对吧？

sentences.en: And I was like, even if we start a new section of the library, like a subnamespace or some kind of naming convention,
sentences.zh: 我说，即使我们开启库的一个新部分，比如一个子命名空间或某种命名约定，

sentences.en: we have all the string algorithms over here in their own little spot.
sentences.zh: 我们把所有的字符串算法都放在那里，在它们自己的小地方。

sentences.en: That beats having, like, to add this to string and then string view and then whatever else comes along later.
sentences.zh: 这比不得不把这些添加到 string，然后是 string_view，然后是以后出现的任何其他东西要好。

sentences.en: Because, you know, sometimes people are going to want to have their own string-like thing.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，有时人们会想要拥有自己的类似字符串的东西。

sentences.en: And it doesn't have to be necessarily interoperable with string or string view.
sentences.zh: 而且它不一定非要与 string 或 string_view 互操作。

sentences.en: And they just can't make it work with generic code without repeating all this API.
sentences.zh: 他们只是无法在不重复所有这些 API 的情况下让它在泛型代码中工作。

sentences.en: And I think that's a huge problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: Like, we want people to write, you know, quick and dirty code that's reusable by everybody as much as they can, right?
sentences.zh: 我们希望人们尽可能多地编写可供所有人复用的、快速且简单的代码，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the testing burden for writing complicated things is so high that we just don't do it, right?
sentences.zh: 因为编写复杂东西的测试负担太高了，以至于我们根本不去写，对吧？

sentences.en: And so you have this untested stuff or you have stuff that just doesn't work in a generic context because either I was going to have to write these extra interfaces and test them.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有这些未经测试的东西，或者在泛型上下文中根本无法工作的东西，因为我要么必须编写这些额外的接口并测试它们。

sentences.en: But since I don't want to do that, I just don't write them or I don't test them.
sentences.zh: 但既然我不想那样做，我就不写它们，或者我不测试它们。

sentences.en: Neither one of those is a very good answer.
sentences.zh: 这两者都不是很好的答案。

sentences.en: This is why, you know, this boost library has steel interfaces and hopefully we're going to standardize this.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么 Boost 库有这些接口，希望我们能将其标准化。

sentences.en: But I have a class in there or a template in there that lets you write iterators much more simply than, like, repeating all the API of an iterator.
sentences.zh: 但我里面有一个类或模板，让你编写迭代器比重复迭代器的所有 API 要简单得多。

sentences.en: Because what I found was I was working on this other library that needed iterators all over the place for views and ranges of things.
sentences.zh: 因为我发现我正在处理另一个需要到处使用迭代器来处理视图和范围的库。

sentences.en: And every time I wrote an iterator, I made, like, a subtle mistake.
sentences.zh: 每次我编写迭代器时，我都会犯一些细微的错误。

sentences.en: And I started realizing I was doing it a lot.
sentences.zh: 我开始意识到我经常这样做。

sentences.en: And so I was like, well, I should have glue for this.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，我应该有胶水代码来处理这个。

sentences.en: This should be easy.
sentences.zh: 这应该很容易。

sentences.en: And so I think we should try to – if we're going to define interfaces that everyone needs to use,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们应该尝试——如果我们打算定义每个人都需要使用的接口，

sentences.en: then we should define either really good glue that helps them generate that code or we should define them in such a minimal way that they don't need to generate that code.
sentences.zh: 那么我们应该定义非常好的胶水代码来帮助他们生成该代码，或者我们应该以一种极简的方式定义它们，使他们不需要生成该代码。

sentences.en: Because all of these bugs that we're introducing, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为我们引入的所有这些 Bug，你知道，

sentences.en: there's something like – I think the industry standard when I learned this back in school was something like for every 100 lines of code, you've got a bug.
sentences.zh: 我想我在学校学到的时候，行业标准大约是每 100 行代码就有一个 Bug。

sentences.en: And that's considered to be a good defect rate.
sentences.zh: 这被认为是很好的缺陷率。

sentences.en: I'm talking about the first draft, right?
sentences.zh: 我说的是初稿，对吧？

sentences.en: So the first time you write some code, people have done some testing and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以你第一次编写代码时，人们已经做了一些测试之类的。

sentences.en: They check it in.
sentences.zh: 他们提交了代码。

sentences.en: And then from that stage, we're not even talking about just I banged out some, you know, bullshit.
sentences.zh: 然后从那个阶段开始，我们甚至不是在谈论我随便写出来的垃圾代码。

sentences.en: Like, this is actually like I've done my due diligence.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是我已经尽职尽责地完成了工作。

sentences.en: I've still got basically a bug every 100 lines.
sentences.zh: 我基本上还是每 100 行代码有一个 Bug。

sentences.en: So if you can reduce the number of lines people write and you reduce the defect rate, that's just like sort of an inherent thing to writing code, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能减少人们编写的代码行数并降低缺陷率，这似乎是编写代码的一种内在特性。

sentences.en: Like, it doesn't seem to depend on the language or anything.
sentences.zh: 它似乎不依赖于语言或其他任何东西。

sentences.en: But right now we have a lot of things, particularly in the standard, that don't lend themselves to reuse that way.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们有很多东西，特别是在标准库中，它们不适合那样复用。

sentences.en: Like, I mean, I know very, very few people have ever written an iterator.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道很少有人写过迭代器。

sentences.en: Like, and you know, whenever I have had to write an iterator, I typically only write the operations that I am going, that I know I will need to use in my code.
sentences.zh: 每当我不得不写迭代器时，我通常只写我知道在我的代码中需要用到的操作。

sentences.en: And it's simply because, like, if I need to show the code to somebody else, I want it to be as, like, short as possible.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是因为，如果我需要把代码展示给别人看，我希望它尽可能短。

sentences.en: And the funny thing is, like, that will not fly with the ranges.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这在 ranges 中行不通。

sentences.en: Right, because the ranges are actually, like, concept-checking.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为 ranges 实际上是在进行概念检查。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know it drives.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道它会驱动……

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a real problem for me.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对我来说是个真正的问题。

sentences.en: Well, you know, in a similar vein, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，同样地，你知道，

sentences.en: there's one of the things that we spend a lot of time talking about when we're designing new library facilities is I think the questions of, like,
sentences.zh: 我们在设计新的库设施时花很多时间讨论的一件事是，我认为关于默认可构造性和类型转换的问题非常多。

sentences.en: default constructability and the conversions that a type has comes up a ton.
sentences.zh: 默认可构造性，即你的东西是否可以被默认构造，通常是你的类型的一个巨大问题。

sentences.en: And, like, default constructability, whether or not your thing can be default constructed, is usually, like, this huge question for your type.
sentences.zh: 因为如果它不能被默认构造，那么在很多上下文中，特别是在泛型代码中，你的东西就无法使用。

sentences.en: Because if it can't be default constructed, then there's a lot of context, especially in generic code, where your thing isn't going to be able to be used.
sentences.zh: 但如果可以，你知道，如果你要让它默认可构造，你的东西是否有某种空状态或未初始化状态？

sentences.en: But if it does, you know, if you are going to make it default constructed, does your thing have some sort of, you know, null state or empty state?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，这对你其余部分的不变性有什么影响？

sentences.en: And if so, what does that do to the invariance of the rest of your thing?
sentences.zh: 同样地，对于转换，你知道，

sentences.en: And likewise, for conversions, you know,
sentences.zh: 关于你的东西何时转换，以及这些转换是隐式的还是显式的，几乎在任何类型的设计中都是一个巨大的问题，特别是当，我认为，

sentences.en: this question of when does your thing convert and are those conversions implicit or explicit is a huge question in the design of almost any type, especially when there's, I think,
sentences.zh: 在委员会中，我们倾向于让任何有性能损失潜力的东西都显式化。

sentences.en: on the committee, we tend to like anything that has potential for performance loss to be explicit.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I remember saying to a bunch of people at committee meeting, we're just hanging out after, you know, sessions.
sentences.zh: 我记得在委员会会议上跟一群人说过，当时我们就在会议间隙闲聊。

sentences.en: And I said, I think I literally said implicit conversions are evil because, like, so many people write so many of them and they cause all kinds of headaches.
sentences.zh: 我当时说，我甚至直言隐式转换是邪恶的，因为太多人写了太多这种转换，导致了各种各样的麻烦。

sentences.en: And then Bjarne, who happened to be there, said, no, they're not evil.
sentences.zh: 然后恰好在场的 Bjarne 说，不，它们并不邪恶。

sentences.en: You just need to make sure that an implicit conversion converts between something that you're converting from and something converting to,
sentences.zh: 你只需要确保隐式转换是在转换源和转换目标之间进行的，

sentences.en: where the to and from types are essentially the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而且转换前后的类型本质上是同一种东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then then it's natural and normal and everybody can can reason about it.
sentences.zh: 那样的话，它就是自然且正常的，每个人都能理解它。

sentences.en: So, like, converting between a float and a double should be implicit for that reason, for instance.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如在 float 和 double 之间进行转换，出于这个原因，应该是隐式的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's questionable.
sentences.zh: 那是值得商榷的。

sentences.en: And I think other languages have made a different decision.
sentences.zh: 我觉得其他语言做出了不同的决定。

sentences.en: I think I like the decision more that an integral value and a floating point value maybe should not be interconvertible.
sentences.zh: 我更倾向于认为整型值和浮点值或许不应该能够相互转换。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But that's a default we have from C.
sentences.zh: 但那是我们从 C 语言继承来的默认行为。

sentences.en: C.
sentences.zh: C 语言。

sentences.en: And I think the question of whether something is default constructible, and by the way, this is another one of the first six pages of EOP is the notion of regularity.
sentences.zh: 关于某物是否应该默认可构造的问题，顺便提一下，这也是《编程要素》（EOP）前六页提到的另一个概念，即“正则性”（regularity）。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like you have all these these operations are like if you're like an end to your regular and that that allows you to reason about your code and in particular to do local reason about your code.
sentences.zh: 就像你拥有的所有这些操作，如果你是一个正则类型，那就能让你对代码进行推理，特别是对代码进行局部推理。

sentences.en: So you don't have to worry about things like the semantics of the code.
sentences.zh: 所以你不必担心代码语义之类的问题。

sentences.en: Plus, where do all these guys live in memory?
sentences.zh: 另外，这些家伙都住在内存的什么地方？

sentences.en: This this one over here, that one over there.
sentences.zh: 这一个在这儿，那一个在那儿。

sentences.en: She lives over here and he lives over there.
sentences.zh: 她住在这儿，他住在那里。

sentences.en: I'm like, I don't know if the alias did the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我心想，我不知道别名是不是也一样。

sentences.en: Like local reasoning is enabled by saying, well, I can see the values and I see how they're used and the semantics of the the operations that I'm doing is I'll have to care about.
sentences.zh: 局部推理之所以可行，是因为我可以看见这些值，看到它们是如何被使用的，我只需要关心我所执行操作的语义。

sentences.en: I don't have to care about lifetime and other things like this.
sentences.zh: 我不需要关心生命周期和其他类似的事情。

sentences.en: So the reason that default constructibility is in there, even though it's not actually required for any of the algorithms in the STL, like everything,
sentences.zh: 所以，默认可构造性之所以包含在内，尽管它实际上并不是 STL 中任何算法所必需的，就像其他所有东西一样，

sentences.en: everything else in regular is actually required to operate with everything in the STL.
sentences.zh: 正则性中的其他一切实际上都是 STL 中所有操作所必需的。

sentences.en: So you can see why that's a useful definition for someone who's going to write something like the STL.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以明白为什么对于编写像 STL 这样东西的人来说，这是一个有用的定义。

sentences.en: So someone asked Alex Stepanoff one time, like, why is that in there?
sentences.zh: 所以曾经有人问 Alex Stepanoff，为什么要把这个放进去？

sentences.en: It's not it's not required, unlike everything else.
sentences.zh: 它不像其他东西那样是必需的。

sentences.en: He said, well, sure, it's convenient.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，当然，这很方便。

sentences.en: And to me, that's that's enough, because, you know, part of that first six pages, he says, like, you know,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就足够了，因为你知道，在那前六页的内容里，他说过，你知道，

sentences.en: you need to not just write like a basis of operations that like could work sometime.
sentences.zh: 你不能只写一套有时能用的基础操作。

sentences.en: And the example he gives is like, what if you have a mathy kind of type?
sentences.zh: 他给出的例子是，如果你有一个数学类型的对象会怎样？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it does arithmetic operations.
sentences.zh: 它执行算术运算。

sentences.en: Well, you could provide like minus, but not plus, like binary minus, but not binary plus.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以提供减法，但不提供加法，比如提供二元减法，但不提供二元加法。

sentences.en: And you could say, well, you just negate it.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，好吧，你只需要把它取反就行了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's in there.
sentences.zh: 是的，它就在那儿。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: OK, you could do that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以那样做。

sentences.en: But it's incredibly inconvenient.
sentences.zh: 但这极其不方便。

sentences.en: It's a it's a it's a type that you want to use for math.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你想用于数学计算的类型。

sentences.en: So you should be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以你应该能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: And I think default constructability goes under the same rubric.
sentences.zh: 我认为默认可构造性也属于同样的范畴。

sentences.en: Like, is it convenient?
sentences.zh: 就像，它方便吗？

sentences.en: And if not, then then why not?
sentences.zh: 如果不是，那为什么不呢？

sentences.en: So I think there are some types that really you cannot default construct because it doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有些类型确实不能默认构造，因为那样没有意义。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So something like a lock.
sentences.zh: 比如锁（lock）。

sentences.en: I know there are patterns that people come up with where like they want a default constructed lock.
sentences.zh: 我知道人们想出了一些模式，想要一个默认构造的锁。

sentences.en: But I think really the ninety nine point nine percent cases, the reason I'm constructing a lock is so that in its lifetime, it holds a lock.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在 99.9% 的情况下，我构造一个锁的原因是希望在它的生命周期内，它能持有一个锁。

sentences.en: And that's what it's for.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的用途。

sentences.en: And it shouldn't do anything else.
sentences.zh: 它不应该做任何其他事情。

sentences.en: So I think that that should be not default constructable.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为它不应该被默认构造。

sentences.en: But I think most things we should definitely have regularity as part of them.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于大多数事物，我们绝对应该将正则性作为其一部分。

sentences.en: And in particular, since that statement from Stepanov, we now have move semantics in the language because that was that was an old interview, I think.
sentences.zh: 特别是自从 Stepanov 那番话之后，我们的语言中现在有了移动语义，因为那是一个旧的访谈，我想。

sentences.en: But now the argument to me is both convenience, the Stepanov answer.
sentences.zh: 但现在对我来说，这个论点既是为了方便，也就是 Stepanov 的答案。

sentences.en: But my new answer is, can you move this thing?
sentences.zh: 但我新的答案是，你能移动这个东西吗？

sentences.en: If you can't move it, then, yeah, let's talk about it, whether it's default constructable.
sentences.zh: 如果你不能移动它，那么好吧，我们可以讨论一下它是否应该默认可构造。

sentences.en: But if you can move it, I don't want to hear this.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能移动它，我不想听这个。

sentences.en: It changes the invariance because the invariance are already that way.
sentences.zh: 它改变了不变性，因为不变性本来就是那样的。

sentences.en: Like you have a move from state that you have to reason about.
sentences.zh: 就像你有一个必须进行推理的“被移动后的状态”。

sentences.en: We don't have, unfortunately, a destroying move operation in C++, where when you move something, it's gone.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，C++ 中没有“销毁式移动”操作，即当你移动某物时，它就消失了。

sentences.en: I don't have to reason about it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不需要再对它进行推理了。

sentences.en: I think that's a better semantic.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是一个更好的语义。

sentences.en: But we don't have that.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有那个。

sentences.en: The fact that I've got this thing around and I have to have that in a set of things that I'm reasoning about when I look at the value because it was moved from,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我身边有这个东西，当我观察这个值时，我必须把它包含在我正在推理的一组事物中，因为它被移动过了，

sentences.en: that means that I have to be able to reason about that before it's got a value as well.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在它拥有值之前，我也必须能够对其进行推理。

sentences.en: So I don't think there's anything wrong or messy about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这并没有什么错误或混乱的地方。

sentences.en: I don't think it weakens invariance in the way that people claim that it does.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它像人们声称的那样削弱了不变性。

sentences.en: I just don't think it's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I tend to agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，我倾向于同意。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I've had the same argument with a lot of people, a lot of very smart people.
sentences.zh: 是的，我和很多人，很多非常聪明的人，都有过同样的争论。

sentences.en: And in some cases, I'm the only one in the discussion that thinks this.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，我是讨论中唯一持这种观点的人。

sentences.en: And so I know it's not a popular opinion amongst especially a lot of the sort of thought leaders in the community, but I really think it's the right answer.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道这不是一个受欢迎的观点，尤其是在社区中许多所谓的思想领袖中间，但我真的认为这是正确的答案。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed and have a great day.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢，祝你有美好的一天。
